top.line: Nadella's insider-risk principles need a written mandate too
top.para: Satya Nadella's 10 October post argues models should be treated as insiders, with seven principles and controls outside the model. This site has argued the same since 30 September. This answer goes principle by principle, separating what runs from design, and adds five missing things, starting with the mandate: observation shows what happened, not whether it was allowed.

s0.line: The argument is mainstream; the products are early
s0.para: Nadella's core move, keeping intelligence and authority over it in different hands, is the enforcer test. Each principle maps to something run, published or planned here, from a second reader to synthetic users. Five gaps decide whether the principles work: the mandate, the deployment, a named owner with expiry, recoverability and speed.

argument.line: Untraceable models need insider-risk controls outside them
argument.para: Frontier model behaviour cannot be traced to code, yet models now act on sensitive data. Nadella keeps responsibility with the deployer, sets alignment aside for engineering, and frames it as insider risk: identity, least privilege, logs, boundaries. Chain-of-thought transparency and models checking models are not enough, so controls must sit outside the model.

seven.line: Each principle maps to running work, with honest limits
seven.para: A second reader on Sonnet checks Opus drafts and fails closed; vaults and append lanes hold tamper-resistant records. Hope or enforcement tested 62 emails, and synthetic users found real bugs, including 51 of 527 missing figures. The site's own ten-rule policy has nine expectations, one setting and no boundary, and near misses should be disclosed.

gaps.line: Five gaps decide whether the seven principles work
gaps.para: Observation needs a mandate written beforehand to judge against. Risk belongs to a deployment, not a model: one customer against 38,000 in Hope or enforcement. Residual risk needs a named owner and an expiry, a brake needs recoverability, and decisions must be made in advance as envelopes, which is also what insurers need.

his.line: Nadella's post covers three areas this work does not
his.para: This work has not addressed chain-of-thought transparency. Its open vocabulary at abp.sgit.ai is mapped to ISO/IEC 42001, OWASP, NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 27001, but a standard needs more than one small company. Continuous adversarial testing at scale needs a vendor with Microsoft's reach.

maturity.line: Much runs today; the rest is design or argued
maturity.para: For each principle, what runs today, what is published as design and what is planned. The second reader, vault ledgers, release checks, synthetic users, read keys, dedicated accounts and incident write-ups run now. The connector twin, plug profile and Licence to Operate are design; automatic revocation and near-miss reporting are planned or argued.

start.line: Start with the mandate, measured reach and counted expectations
start.para: Write and lock the mandate before the agent runs, measure the reach and derive the gap. Mark each rule by its enforcer and count the expectations, add a second reader on irreversible actions, journal connector calls, name an owner and expiry, and publish near misses. Knowing how little to trust a model lets it do more.

sources.line: Sources: Nadella's post and this network's linked articles
sources.para: Satya Nadella's post of 10 October 2026, paraphrased and quoted once, checked by an agent in a separate session and rewritten by this site's agent. Links include The ultimate insider, Hope or enforcement, the second reader article, the connector twin, RiskMandate pages, abp.sgit.ai and NASA's Aviation Safety Reporting System.
